title: WERE THERE NO GRAVES IN EGYPT?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"They said to Moses, 'Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you
brought us to the desert to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of
Egypt? Didn't we say to you in Egypt, "Leave us alone; let us serve the
Egyptians"? It would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die
in the desert!'" - Ex 14:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The prayer turns to bitterness quickly. And notice their memory has already
started rewriting itself.

"It would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians." Really? Days ago they
were groaning under slavery. Now, with danger in front of them, Egypt suddenly
looks tolerable.

This is what fear does to memory. It makes the past look safer than it was. The
enemy of our souls uses this constantly. He shows us the food of Egypt and hides
the whips. He reminds us of the comfort of an old habit and edits out the
misery it caused.

There is also a sharp accusation here: "What have you done to us?" Moses is
blamed for obeying God.

Yet notice something remarkable. God does not strike them down for this. In the
very next verses He answers with reassurance and then with deliverance. Their
panic did not disqualify them.

That is grace. Psalm 103:14 says, "He knows how we are formed, he remembers that
we are dust." God's patience with frightened, complaining people is one of the
great themes of this book.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your memory making some part of your old life look better than it was?
2. Have you blamed someone for a difficulty God allowed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, guard my memory from lying to me about what You rescued me from. Thank
You for Your patience when I panic. Amen.
